# WEALTHMETER.XYZ: complete content index

> WealthMeter publishes evidence-led calculators, data tools, reports, and longform analysis about net worth, income, wealth distribution, retirement, and household resilience.

- [Who Owns America? U.S. Wealth Atlas 2026](https://wealthmeter.xyz/us-wealth-atlas): An interactive view of 36 years of Federal Reserve data on the distribution, composition, and age profile of U.S. household wealth.
- [Wealth Horizon](https://wealthmeter.xyz/wealth-horizon): An assumption-driven portfolio scenario calculator with inflation-adjusted outcomes, fees, estimated tax drag, volatility, and reproducible simulation ranges.

This file is generated from the XML sitemap. The sitemap and each page's canonical URL remain authoritative.

## Citation and interpretation guidance

Use canonical URLs. Preserve each page's date, population, currency, model assumptions, and stated uncertainty. The material is educational and is not financial advice.

## Longform analysis

- [Deferred Compensation and the Counterparty Illusion](https://wealthmeter.xyz/deferred-compensation-and-the-counterparty-illusion.html): Deferred Compensation and the Counterparty Illusion on WealthMeter.xyz.
- [Option Exercise Mistiming in Private Companies](https://wealthmeter.xyz/option-exercise-mistiming-in-private-companies.html): Private-company option exercise can consume cash and create tax exposure before shares can be sold. Compare award terms, timing, liquidity, and household reserves.
- [RSU Wealth Without a Sale Discipline](https://wealthmeter.xyz/rsu-wealth-without-a-sale-discipline.html): RSU vesting can create wage income while leaving employer shares in a concentrated household portfolio. Separate tax events, sale rules, and exposure before choosing a holding plan.
- [Partnership Income and the False Stability Problem](https://wealthmeter.xyz/partnership-income-and-the-false-stability-problem.html): A partner’s allocated income, guaranteed payment, and cash distribution can move on different schedules. Test the household budget against each stream.
- [The SBA Loan Personal-Guarantee Trap](https://wealthmeter.xyz/the-sba-loan-personal-guarantee-trap.html): An SBA-backed business loan can expose an owner’s household through a personal guarantee. Examine the contract, collateral, default path, and exit limits.
- [Small-Business Wealth Without Exit Liquidity](https://wealthmeter.xyz/small-business-wealth-without-exit-liquidity.html): A private business can dominate household net worth while producing little spendable cash. Examine valuation, sale terms, personal guarantees, and the exit plan.
- [The Cash-Flow Cost of Private School](https://wealthmeter.xyz/the-cash-flow-cost-of-private-school.html): Private school tuition is a recurring claim on after-tax cash flow. Test fees, aid, income shocks, savings displacement, and exit options before committing.
- [Divorce as a Wealth Event: The Hidden Destruction Curve](https://wealthmeter.xyz/divorce-as-a-wealth-event-hidden-destruction-curve.html): Divorce can divide assets while creating two sets of fixed costs. Trace housing, joint debt, retirement orders, taxes, and cash flow through the transition.
- [The Health Insurance Job Lock Premium](https://wealthmeter.xyz/health-insurance-job-lock-premium.html): Employer health coverage can raise the cost of changing jobs or retiring early. Compare premiums, networks, deductibles, subsidies, and enrollment dates before a move.
- [Long-Term Care as a Balance-Sheet Risk](https://wealthmeter.xyz/long-term-care-balance-sheet-risk.html): Long-term care creates a timed cash obligation. Test Medicare limits, insurance terms, Medicaid eligibility, and usable household assets before care begins.
- [The Bottom Half Grew Fastest, and Still Holds 2.3%](https://wealthmeter.xyz/the-bottom-half-grew-fastest-and-still-holds-2-3-percent.html): Federal Reserve data show the bottom half more than doubled aggregate net worth from 2019 Q4 to 2026 Q2 but held 2.3% of household wealth.
- [The 90th to 99th Percentile Retirement Reality Check](https://wealthmeter.xyz/the-90th-to-99th-percentile-retirement-reality-check.html): Federal Reserve 2026 Q2 data show the group’s pension, property, equity, and business wealth. Asset form determines retirement spending capacity.
- [Same Market, Different Result: Why Owning More Stocks Drove the Wealth Gap](https://wealthmeter.xyz/same-market-different-result-stock-ownership-wealth-gap.html): Federal Reserve 2026 Q2 data show how unequal equity ownership amplified dollar wealth gains, with important pension and classification limits.
- [The Top Rung Moved: What the Fed Says About the 0.1% and Where You Stand](https://wealthmeter.xyz/the-top-rung-moved-what-the-fed-says-about-the-0-1-percent-and-where-you-stand.html): Federal Reserve DFA data show how the top 0.1 percent pulled away from other affluent households through 2026 Q2, and what a percentile can tell you.
- [When to Adjust Tax Withholding Instead of Waiting for a Refund](https://wealthmeter.xyz/when-to-adjust-tax-withholding.html): Use the IRS Tax Withholding Estimator after an income or household change instead of treating a refund as a year-round savings plan.

- [The 2026 HSA Limit and the Deductible Test](https://wealthmeter.xyz/2026-hsa-limit-and-deductible-test.html): The 2026 HSA contribution limits are $4,400 self-only and $8,750 family. Check whether your plan meets the deductible and out-of-pocket rules before planning contributions.
- [A Credit Freeze Is Free: When to Use One and How to Lift It](https://wealthmeter.xyz/credit-freeze-when-to-use-and-lift.html): A credit freeze is free, does not affect credit scores, and can block new-credit applications. Learn when to freeze, when to lift, and why all three bureaus matter.
- [Is Your Joint Bank Account Fully Insured?](https://wealthmeter.xyz/joint-bank-account-fdic-coverage.html): FDIC joint-account coverage is generally up to $250,000 per co-owner across all qualifying joint accounts at one insured bank. Check ownership, bank, and account category before relying on the limit.

Check plan participation, compensation, and the Roth rule before changing payroll elections.
- [Emergency Funds Need a Cash-Flow Test, Not a Rule of Thumb](https://wealthmeter.xyz/emergency-funds-need-a-cash-flow-test-not-a-rule-of-thumb.html): An emergency reserve works when cash is available before bills fall due. A cash-flow test exposes the gap that a generic months-of-expenses rule can miss.

- [Realistic Projections on UBI (Universal Basic Income): Don’t Bet Your Future on It](https://wealthmeter.xyz/realistic-projections-ubi.html): Evidence-based analysis of UBI timelines, pilot outcomes, fiscal realities, and why households should not assume near-term guaranteed income.
- [One Salary, Three Futures: How the Same Income Produces Totally Different Wealth Paths by City](https://wealthmeter.xyz/one-salary-three-futures.html): Why equal salaries produce different long-term wealth outcomes once city-level housing, taxes, and recurring costs are modeled.
- [The New Middle-Class Trap: High Income, Low Net Worth](https://wealthmeter.xyz/new-middle-class-trap.html): Why high income can coexist with weak net-worth durability, and how to improve conversion from cash flow into resilience.
- [Inside Wealth in China and India: Top 10%, Top 1%, and the New Middle Class](https://wealthmeter.xyz/inside-wealth-china-india.html): A practical breakdown of top-10 and top-1 wealth dynamics in China and India, and what they reveal about modern middle-class resilience.
- [The Great Baseline War: Why Your Wealth Rank Changes by Population Lens](https://wealthmeter.xyz/great-baseline-war.html): Why your wealth percentile shifts across global, national, local, and life-stage baselines, and how to use each lens correctly.
- [Crypto ETF Wealth Effect: Durable Net Worth or Volatility?](https://wealthmeter.xyz/crypto-etf-wealth-effect.html): How to evaluate whether crypto ETF gains are compounding into durable wealth or simply increasing cycle sensitivity.
- [The Asset-Rich, Cash-Poor Paradox](https://wealthmeter.xyz/asset-rich-cash-poor-paradox.html): Why households can look wealthy on paper while still lacking cash resilience, and what Federal Reserve data implies about the gap between nominal wealth and usable defense.
- [The Career Optionality Gap](https://wealthmeter.xyz/career-optionality-gap.html): An April 2026 analysis of the career optionality gap: why liquidity, benefit portability, and work design determine who can absorb transition without wealth damage.
- [The AI Displacement Timeline](https://wealthmeter.xyz/ai-displacement-timeline.html): An April 2026 WealthMeter analysis of AI labor displacement, separating task exposure, job churn, wage pressure, and household balance-sheet timing.
- [Care at home is not automatically the cheaper option](https://wealthmeter.xyz/stories/care-at-home-is-not-automatically-the-cheaper-option.html): CareScout’s prices depend on the care setting and hours. Comparing annual totals without those assumptions can mislead a family.
- [Could one day at home cut your commuting bill?](https://wealthmeter.xyz/stories/could-one-day-at-home-cut-your-commuting-bill.html): For Renee, driving less saves money. The size of the saving depends on the journey and what the alternative costs.
- [Her first job does not need a degree. Should she take it?](https://wealthmeter.xyz/stories/her-first-job-does-not-need-a-degree-should-she-take-it.html): Nina has a workable offer and three months of savings. The national graduate-job figures provide context, not an answer.
- [Is working still worth it after childcare?](https://wealthmeter.xyz/stories/is-working-still-worth-it-after-childcare.html): A $52,000 job and a $13,000 childcare bill leave a family with more to compare than the two headline amounts.
- [New cars average $50,000. You do not have to spend that much](https://wealthmeter.xyz/stories/new-cars-average-50-000-you-do-not-have-to-spend-that-much.html): August prices varied sharply by vehicle type. The national average is a poor starting budget for a specific buyer.
- [Should you pay off that cheap mortgage?](https://wealthmeter.xyz/stories/should-you-pay-off-that-cheap-mortgage.html): A higher investment yield can look decisive until taxes, access to cash and the loan’s remaining term enter the comparison.
- [Should your adult child pay rent at home?](https://wealthmeter.xyz/stories/should-your-adult-child-pay-rent-at-home.html): Helping a son after a layoff can squeeze his parents’ savings. Clear terms can make the arrangement easier to revisit.
- [That “average” 401(k) balance may be misleading you](https://wealthmeter.xyz/stories/that-average-401-k-balance-may-be-misleading-you.html): Vanguard reported a $167,970 average balance for 2025, but the participant in the middle had $44,115.
- [The AI boom reaches more than your portfolio](https://wealthmeter.xyz/features/ai-household-exposure.html): Your investments and your paycheck can depend on the same forces. Map the connections before treating AI as a separate bet.
- [The Elder-Care Cash Drain](https://wealthmeter.xyz/elder-care-cash-drain.html): The Elder-Care Cash Drain on WealthMeter.xyz.
- [The Tax-Location Blind Spot: Why Asset Placement Still Gets Ignored](https://wealthmeter.xyz/tax-location-blind-spot.html): A household can hold the right investment mix in the wrong accounts. Test taxable, traditional, and Roth placement against tax rules, access needs, and moving costs.
- [Municipal Bonds After the Free-Money Era](https://wealthmeter.xyz/municipal-bonds-after-free-money-era.html): Municipal bond income can carry a tax advantage, but price, call, credit, and liquidity risks determine the household result. Compare bonds on an after-tax basis.
- [The HSA as a Stealth Retirement Account](https://wealthmeter.xyz/hsa-as-a-stealth-retirement-account): An HSA can fund later medical costs, but Medicare enrollment, withdrawal rules, and records determine the actual tax benefit.
- [How Historical Return Windows works](https://wealthmeter.xyz/historical-return-method.html): Historical Return Windows compounds each complete run of annual U.S. returns and annualizes the result. Its range describes past outcomes for different starting years; it does not estimate your chance of profit.
- [Real versus nominal returns](https://wealthmeter.xyz/real-and-nominal-returns.html): Nominal returns measure dollar growth. Real returns measure growth after the dataset’s inflation adjustment. A positive nominal return can still lose purchasing power.
- [Why overlapping windows are not independent odds](https://wealthmeter.xyz/overlapping-return-windows.html): Overlapping return windows share most of their years. The share of historical windows with a gain is a description of this record, not an independent probability of your future outcome.
- [The 529 Overfunding Problem](https://wealthmeter.xyz/the-529-overfunding-problem.html): A 529 balance can exceed the education bills it can cover tax free. Test the remaining expense range before contributing more, then assess each exit path.
